key_insight: The paper couples phase-field fracture with discrete differential geometry so crack growth and large shape change are solved together on the same thin-structure surface.
engineering_relevance: It enables more realistic design and failure prediction for flexible, highly deformable structures such as thin films and flexible electronics.
method: Triangulated midsurface DDG model for membrane and bending energy
Phase field defined on the discrete surface with staggered, irreversibility-enforced solve
Element deletion and topology reconstruction to allow full crack opening and large post-fracture reconfiguration
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with geometrically nonlinear finite element results in 2D and successful reproduction of 3D tearing phenomena, including crack convergence/coalescence and flexible-electronics-like island-bridge behavior.
watch_item: The degradation-deletion plus topology reconstruction workflow may add implementation complexity and can be sensitive near nearly failed elements or rapidly changing crack paths.
paper_title: Phase-Field Fracture Simulation of Highly Deformable Thin Structures via a Discrete Differential Geometry Framework
